fixes.explanation: Seven laps is a Jericho special, baker. There the people marched around the city once a day for six days, and on the seventh day they went around it seven times (Joshua 6:14, 15). That's a lot of steps, and I bet somebody wished for a step counter. Ai gets a different plan. The LORD tells Joshua, "Set up an ambush behind the city."

That's right, baker. Joshua tells the men in ambush to rise up and take the city while Israel is fleeing, because the LORD their God will deliver it into their hands (Joshua 8:7). Then the LORD tells Joshua to hold out his battle lance toward Ai, and as soon as he does, the men in ambush rise quickly (Joshua 8:18, 19). Timing matters. Nobody wants to pop out of the closet before the surprise party starts.

That number belongs to the first try at Ai. About three thousand men went up then, and they fled before the men of Ai (Joshua 7:4). This time the LORD tells Joshua, Israel's leader, “Take the whole army with you…” It's like me trying to press a whole holiday order with one worn-out stamp. Same small effort, same blurry result. Israel isn't sent back with the same small crew.

Search? Nobody's rummaging around for lost keys here. Joshua's order is “…set it on fire.” When the men in ambush take the city, they don't stop to look around. They set it on fire right away (Joshua 8:19).

North, baker! The troops “…camped to the north of it, with the valley between them and the city.” That's the group out front in plain view. The other group sits hidden to the west, between Bethel and Ai (Joshua 8:12). One crew waves hello while the other waits quietly, and the king of Ai did not know about the ambush (Joshua 8:14).

Not quite, baker. The king of Ai sees the Israelites and hurries out early in the morning to meet them in battle. But the text says “…he did not know that an ambush had been set up against him behind the city.” He's staring at the army in front of him while the surprise sits behind him.
